title: Dip to black and Dip to white visibly fade out and fade back in
goal: A dip should read as a fade: the outgoing clip fades down to black (or white), holds if asked, then the next clip fades up out of it. Today the user sees the picture jump straight to black or white and then jump straight to the next clip, with no fade either way, so the transition looks like two hard cuts.
notes:
User's words: "when i dip to black, there is no fade out and fade in. It just goes to black and then to the new clip." then "same with white".

From code reading (not run): the model does ramp. ClipTransition.dipAmount (PhotonzCore/ClipTransitions.swift:199-210) rises over beforeMS to the cut, holds holdMS at 1, falls over afterMS. Used for a cut inside a clip (ClipTransitions.swift:483, panel at :542 via dipPanel :565-575, a full-frame rectangle layer at that opacity) and for an edit point between two clips (EditPointTransitions.swift:245, panel inserted :307). Sound uses it too (TransitionSound.swift:46).
Suspects, NOT confirmed, reproduce first: (1) default length 400 ms (ClipTransition.defaultLengthMS, :112) is split across the cut, so 200 ms down and 200 ms up, which at playback reads as a jump; (2) the playback path draws frames without the dip panel opacity (or only at whole-clip boundaries), while scrub/export are right; (3) at an edit point between two separate clips, the incoming clip starts drawing over the panel or the panel sits under it (insert at index + 1 ordering); (4) with a hold, the panel order or timing around the moved clip start. Existing walks with dips: transitions-at-a-cut-walk, transition-placement-and-hold-walk, transition-carries-the-sound-walk; check whether any of them measures frames mid-fade during PLAYBACK (likely not).
acceptance: Reproduce first at Next defaults, in the user's setup: two clips back to back on the timeline with Dip to black between them (and a cut inside one recording too), at the default length and with a hold. Watch it PLAY in the editor, scrub it, and export it. Record in the audit which of those shows hard jumps, and photograph frames at 25/50/75% of the fade down and the fade up

MEASURED in the audit: mean luminance of the picture at 10 evenly spaced moments across the fade down and the fade up, for playback (frames as shown on the canvas during play), scrubbing and export. Each must change smoothly (no step bigger than a third of the range between neighbouring samples) for Dip to black and Dip to white

If the default length is the problem (today 400 ms in all, so 0.2 s each way), the default becomes long enough to read as a fade (for example 1 s, 0.5 s each way) and the Length menu says the fade length in plain words; the change is justified with the frames in the audit
The fade down uses the outgoing clip and the fade up uses the incoming clip; the hold, if any, is solid colour between them
The sound dips with it as it does today
A walk at Next defaults plays a dip to black and a dip to white between two clips and records frames during playback, failing if any step is bigger than the bound above
Audit under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

log.note: Reproduced at Next defaults (probe, screen unlocked, Screen Recording granted): with the 0.4s default a Dip to black between two clips ramps correctly when stopped, playing and exported (6.8s..7.2s every 40 ms: 0.30 0.24 0.18 0.12 0.06 0.00 0.06 ... 0.30), so suspects 2-4 (playback path, panel order, hold) are ruled out. The real cause is suspect 1: 0.2s each way is about six frames and plays as two cuts.

Adversarial pass: Premiere and Final Cut default a new transition to 1s, and the transition mock's dip reads 1.0s ('A fades out inside its own last half second and B fades in inside its own first half second'). So a NEW dip now defaults to 1000 ms (ClipTransitionKind.defaultLengthMS; ClipTransition.init with no length and ClipCut.fitted use it). An existing transition keeps its length when its kind changes, as Premiere does. The overlap kinds stay at 400 ms because each extra ms is spare media spent; whether to raise them is asked in the audit.

Shipped: Length menu choices on a dip read '1.0s, 0.5s out and 0.5s in' (ClipTransitionCopy.lengthChoice); measureFade gained 'smooth' (FadeRamp: no neighbour step > 1/3 of the range, for stopped, played and export); new walk a-dip-fades-out-and-back-in-walk at Next defaults measures Dip to black, Dip to white, a 1s white hold and a dip on a cut inside one recording. The spare-strip label now starts past the band edge, because the wider band covered it. Tests: DipLengthTests and FadeRampTests. Full suite 11228 green. Walks green: the new one, transition-carries-the-sound, transitions-where-clips-meet, transition-placement-and-hold, transitions-at-a-cut, default-transition-key, transition-on-every-cut, transition-edge-follows-the-pointer.

Rough items: dissolve default length is a question in the audit's evaluate list (no task, since the user decides). The mock's dip paragraph is not printed, covered by UX-PATTERNS §4. Nothing filed: nothing left clears the follow-up bar.
